statement: A British Museum indexed object record describes a large carved cocha vessel, accession Am1991,Q.4, as late fifteenth-century Inca, likely associated with the Coricancha precinct; the museum proposes possible liquid-offering use but states the original context as probable rather than proven.

sources.citation: British Museum, vessel/cocha, Am1991,Q.4, object catalog and curatorial comment, https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/E_Am1991-Q-4
sources.author: British Museum curatorial inventory
sources.access_note: Indexed full object description accessible in search output; opening the museum URL returned HTTP 403. Provenance is described as unknown; the Coricancha placement and function are explicitly proposed, not demonstrated.

does_not_demonstrate: A proposed association with Coricancha does not establish actual placement or original ritual use.
Late fifteenth-century dating applies to the museum's object interpretation, not the creation of the wider Inca religious system.
No unsupported links to specific sacrifice rites, temple inventory or universal state practice are inferred.
adversarial_counter: Missing acquisition/provenance history and proposed rather than documented temple context limit object-based generalization.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
